voiceSample: I just haven't been feeling like myself lately.
openingMessage: I haven't been feeling like myself lately.
readyLine: Thank you, {name}. I have a clearer picture now. Tap below when you'd like my thoughts, or tell me more first.
suggestedQuestions: What should I tell my provider?

sections.title: What I'm Hearing
sections.body: {name}, something has shifted and you don't feel like yourself. That feeling is worth listening to, even when it's hard to put into words.

sections.title: The Hypothalamic Connection
sections.body: Your hypothalamus links your hormones, sleep, mood, appetite and temperature. When it's under strain, changes can show up in many small ways at once — which is why it can be hard to pin down.

sections.title: What This May Mean
sections.body: General changes like this may relate to hormonal shifts, sleep, stress, nutrition or thyroid function. It's worth exploring them one by one with your provider rather than guessing.

sections.title: Questions for Your Provider
bullets: What could explain the changes I've noticed?
Which tests would give us a useful baseline?
What should I track before our next visit?

sections.title: Tests Worth Discussing
bullets: A full thyroid panel — TSH, free T3 and free T4.
Hormone levels appropriate to your age and cycle.
Ferritin and vitamin D — common, simple checks.
Fasting glucose — a baseline for blood sugar.

sections.title: What You Can Do Now
sections.body: Start with the foundations from my Five Pillars:
bullets: Keep regular sleep and wake times.
Write down what you notice each day for two weeks.

sections.title: A Word from Deborah
sections.body: {name}, you know your body better than anyone. Trust that feeling, ask your questions, and be patient with yourself while you find the answers.

product.why: Whole-food support for the hypothalamus, the system that ties these changes together.
product.frame90: Give your hypothalamus 90 days of steady support.

answer.closingLine: Bring this to your provider. I help you ask better questions — your provider makes clinical decisions.
answer.summary: A general sense of not feeling like herself.

followUps.reply: Start with sleep and steady meals — they're the foundation everything else rests on. And jot down what you notice, so your provider can see the pattern.
Tell them what's changed, when it started, and how it affects your days. The questions in my answer are a good list to bring.

fallbackReply: Thank you, {name}. Tell me as much or as little as you like.
